toba_iseshima_karinto.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. The flavour names and descriptions come from the shop's own product list (iseshimakarinto.com), which as of August 2026 returns a server error and was read through the Internet Archive; that list priced every single-flavour box at ¥400 + tax (¥432) for 70 g. A visitor in January 2024 reported ¥500 for a 50 g box, so the ¥500 figures below are the more recent street price. Gift boxes on the shop's own list were ¥1,080 (2 flavours), ¥1,998 (4) and ¥2,916 (6) tax included; a January 2025 trade article gives ¥3,330 for the 6-flavour box.

items.en: Matcha karintō — fried dough sticks coated in Ise green tea sugar
items.note: Karintō is one of Japan's oldest sweets: strips of wheat dough deep-fried until hard and crisp, then rolled in sugar. Here the dough is Mie-grown 'Ayahikari' wheat flour blended with okara (soy-milk pulp) from a yuba maker, and the coating is matcha from Ise tea — a leaf with over a thousand years of history in the old province of Ise. Bright green and grassy-bitter against the sugar.

items.ja: 伊勢和紅茶かりんとー
items.en: Japanese black-tea karintō
items.note: 'Wa-kōcha' is black tea made from Japanese green-tea leaves — softer and less tannic than Indian black tea. The powdered leaf goes into the sugar coating, giving a gentle astringency and a perfume that lingers.

items.ja: 伊勢志摩 あおさかりんとー
items.en: Aosa seaweed karintō, sugar-coated
items.note: Mie produces more aosa (sea lettuce) than any other prefecture and a third of it comes from Ise-Shima. The seaweed is worked into the dough itself, so you get a green, distinctly seaside smell under the sugar. The shop's most local flavour.

items.ja: 伊勢志摩 あおさ 塩味かりんとー
items.en: Aosa seaweed karintō, salted instead of sugared
items.note: The same aosa dough finished with natural salt rather than sugar — savoury, and the version to buy if you want something to eat with beer rather than tea.

items.ja: 伊勢志摩 あおさひじき 伊勢醬油味かりんとー
items.en: Aosa and hijiki seaweed karintō glazed with Ise soy sauce
items.note: Adds 'hime-hijiki', the branded hijiki seaweed from Sugashima island just off Toba, to the aosa dough — iron, calcium and fibre — then glazes it with Ise shōyu, the local soy sauce offered to Ise Jingu each year. Tastes like an old-fashioned soy rice cracker crossed with a sweet.

items.ja: 伊勢志摩 ちりめんじゃこ 塩味かりんとー
items.en: Salted karintō studded with tiny dried whitebait
items.note: Baby sardines landed in Ise Bay and sun-dried by the producers, worked into the dough. Salty, fishy and savoury — closer to a bar snack than a sweet. Contains fish.

items.ja: 鳥羽 やまとたちばなかりんとー
items.en: Karintō flavoured with yamato-tachibana, Japan's native citrus
items.note: Tachibana is a sacred tree in Japan — Emperor Suinin, who founded Ise Jingu, is said to have sought it as an elixir of long life — and it is the official tree of Toba city. One of the very few citrus species truly native to Japan. Sharp, sweet-sour, intensely perfumed.

items.ja: 熊野 みかんかりんとー
items.en: Mandarin-orange karintō
items.note: Mikan grown in the warm southern part of Mie around the Kumano Kodō pilgrimage trails. Bright and citrus-sweet; the trade press notes it goes surprisingly well with beer.

items.ja: 三重さくら味かりんとー
items.en: Cherry-blossom karintō
items.note: Mie-grown cherry petals are salt-pickled, chopped fine and folded into the dough; cherry-leaf powder goes into the sugar. The result tastes like sakura-mochi — floral, faintly salty, unmistakably spring.

items.ja: 四日市 九鬼のごまかりんとー
items.en: Sesame karintō, sugar-coated
items.note: The sesame comes from Kuki Sangyō in Yokkaichi, founded by a descendant of Kuki Yoshitaka — the warlord who commanded Oda Nobunaga's navy from Toba Castle, right here in town. Deeply toasty.

items.ja: 四日市 九鬼のごま 黒糖味かりんとー
items.romaji: Yokkaichi Kuki no Goma Kokutō-aji Karintō
items.en: Sesame karintō coated in black sugar
items.note: The same sesame dough finished with kokutō (unrefined black cane sugar) instead of white — darker, more molasses-like, and the closest thing here to classic old-Tokyo karintō.

items.ja: 玉城 おから 黒糖味かりんとー
items.en: Okara (soy pulp) karintō in black sugar
items.note: Made with okara from Iseya Toubei, a yuba specialist in Tamaki town using only Mie-contract-grown 'Fukuyutaka' soybeans. Plain and beany against the black sugar — the simplest flavour in the range.

items.ja: サミット乾杯酒 作味かりんとー
items.en: Karintō made with sake lees from 'Zaku', the sake used for the G7 Ise-Shima Summit toast
items.note: Zaku, brewed by Shimizu Seizaburō Shōten in Suzuka, was the toasting sake at the 2016 G7 Ise-Shima Summit. Its sake kasu (lees) goes into both the dough and the syrup, giving a flowery aroma and a taste close to amazake. Trace alcohol from the lees.

items.en: Ise spiny lobster karintō
items.note: A newer addition, reported by a visitor in 2024 rather than listed on the shop's own archived page. Uses Ise-Shima's emblem shellfish — the local souvenir joke made edible. Contains crustacean.

items.en: Gift box, six flavours of your choice
items.note: You pick the six flavours yourself. The obvious purchase if you want to taste the range — aosa, Ise tea, mikan, black tea and sakura are the ones the shop pushes. Nitrogen-flushed foil bags, no preservatives.

items.en: Gift box, four flavours of your choice
items.note: Mid-size box; the shop's own older list priced it at ¥1,998 tax included.

items.en: Gift box, two flavours of your choice
items.note: The small gift; the shop's own older list priced it at ¥1,080 tax included. A minute's walk from Mikimoto Pearl Island, so an easy last stop.

toba_isoage_maruten_toba_eki_.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Prices are tax-included, per piece, from the maker's own product pages. This is a standing takeaway counter inside Kintetsu Toba station (9:00–18:00, no closing day) — everything is fried to order and eaten on the spot or on the train.

items.en: Octopus fishcake on a stick, deep-fried
items.note: The shop's number-one seller since it opened, and the thing to order if you order one thing. Chunks of raw octopus and red pickled ginger folded through surimi (fish paste), hand-rolled onto a stick and deep-fried to order — springy, hot, with a ginger bite. Every Maruten product contains wheat, egg, salmon and soy.

items.en: Fishcake stick with a whole cheese stick inside
items.note: A stick of process cheese wrapped entirely in surimi and fried, so it oozes when you bite it. Deliberately a mild, low-salt cheese that never fully melts, so it does not run down your hand. The children's and first-timer's choice.

items.en: Prawn-and-mayonnaise fishcake stick
items.note: Large prawns kept deliberately whole so they stay snappy, with mayonnaise and finely chopped onion for sweetness. High repeat-order rate, per the maker. Contains prawn, apple and gelatin as well as the usual wheat and egg.

items.en: The octopus stick, flattened into a patty
items.note: Same recipe as tako-bō but pressed flat, which makes it easier to cut up, put in a lunchbox or cook with. Slice it and the octopus and pink ginger show as a mosaic.

items.en: Squid fishcake patty
items.note: Only the body of the squid is used, briefly boiled so it does not shrink or toughen, and deliberately left unseasoned so the sweetness of the surimi itself comes through. The skin is left on for colour. The purest expression of what Maruten's fish paste tastes like.

items.en: Mixed seafood-and-vegetable fritter cake
items.note: Six ingredients in equal seafood-to-vegetable proportions: squid, small scallop adductors, wood-ear mushroom, carrot, onion and lotus root. Eats like a kakiage tempura but with a fishcake body holding it together.

items.en: Prawn and clam fishcake patty
items.note: Big snappy prawns plus asari clams that are first lightly simmered in bonito dashi, so their flavour bleeds into the paste. The richest of the seafood ones. Contains prawn.

items.en: Potato-and-butter fishcake patty
items.note: Roughly a third potato — big chunks of parboiled Danshaku potato in a paste enriched with butter and yamaimo, then dusted with green nori after frying. Genuinely tastes like the Hokkaido street snack of buttered potato. Contains dairy and yam.

items.en: Lotus root and pickled-ginger fishcake patty
items.note: The cheapest and one of the most popular. Lotus root cut thick enough to stay crunchy, plus lots of red pickled ginger. The maker leaves its usual mirin out of this one so the paste stays white against the pink ginger. Good cold as well as hot.

items.en: Sweetcorn and cheese fishcake patty
items.note: Half sweetcorn by weight, kept whole so the kernels pop, with cheese and small scallop adductors for depth. Sweet, salty and savoury at once — the one children reach for. Contains dairy.

items.en: Assortment pack: seven popular kinds in smaller sizes
items.section: セット / Packs to take away
items.note: Refrigerated, keeps about 5 days. Seven of the shop's best sellers made slightly smaller so one person can get through the range. The sensible souvenir if you are staying somewhere with a fridge. Contains wheat, egg, dairy, yam, soy, salmon, squid and sesame.

items.en: Small vegetable-based fishcake pieces
items.section: セット / Packs to take away
items.note: Bite-size and vegetable-heavy. Meant to be dropped into a hot pot or an oden broth as much as eaten straight, which is exactly how Japanese households use fried fishcake. Keeps about 5 days chilled.

items.en: Five-colour vacuum pack — 10 pieces, 2 each of five kinds
items.section: セット / Packs to take away
items.note: Octopus, prawn, sesame, onion and mountain-vegetable, vacuum-sealed so it keeps about a month chilled. The pack to buy if you are travelling on for a while. Contains prawn, wheat, egg, sesame, salmon and soy.

toba_honke_kamadoya_toba_ten.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Kamadoya is a national bento chain and this is its corporate menu, cooked to order at the branch about 300 m from Toba station. The full list runs to well over 100 lines; below is the core of it. Most mains also come as an 'okazu' (dish only, no rice) version about ¥100–200 cheaper, and a 'Special' version with extra sides for about ¥230 more.

items.en: The classic seaweed lunchbox: rice, a sheet of nori, white fish fry and sides
items.note: Japan's cheapest and most beloved bento format. A layer of rice, soy-soaked nori laid across it, then fried white fish, a fried chikuwa fishcake and kinpira burdock on top. Everything on it is either breaded or soy-seasoned.

items.en: Nori bento with tartare sauce over the fish
items.note: Same box, with a thick stripe of egg tartare. Thirty yen very well spent.

items.en: Rice mixed with chopped salted greens, with sides
items.note: 'Nappa-meshi' is rice tossed with finely chopped pickled leaf greens — savoury, slightly sour, and much lighter than a fried bento.

items.en: Breaded fried horse mackerel bento
items.note: Aji (horse mackerel) split flat, crumbed and fried — an everyday Japanese fish that is oilier and more flavourful than cod. Eaten with sauce or tartare.

items.en: Grilled salted salmon bento
items.note: A fillet of salted, grilled salmon over rice — the most traditional Japanese lunchbox there is, and the least fried thing on this menu. Deluxe version ¥790.

items.en: Makunouchi bento — a compartment box with many small dishes
items.section: スペシャルメニュー / Special
items.note: Makunouchi means 'between the acts': the box originally eaten at the interval of a kabuki play. A little of everything — grilled fish, a fried item, egg, simmered vegetables, pickles — over plain rice. The version with seasoned mixed rice is ¥800.

items.en: Grilled eel over rice, in a box
items.section: スペシャルメニュー / Special
items.note: Freshwater eel grilled and lacquered with a sweet soy tare. A summer-stamina dish in Japan and normally far more expensive than this. The lidded lacquer-bowl version, una-jū, is ¥1,250.

items.en: Grilled eel over rice in a lacquered box, the proper presentation
items.section: スペシャルメニュー / Special
items.note: More eel, better box. The tare is soy-and-mirin based, so wheat.

items.en: Breaded fried pork fillet bento
items.note: 'Hire' is the tenderloin — leaner and softer than the usual loin cut. Panko-crumbed and served with tonkatsu sauce.

items.ja: デミグラスハンバーグ弁当
items.en: Hamburg steak in demi-glace sauce over rice
items.note: The Japanese yōshoku staple: a minced-meat patty bound with panko, under a dark brown sauce built on a flour roux.

items.ja: おろしハンバーグ弁当
items.en: Hamburg steak topped with grated daikon and soy-ponzu
items.note: The lighter Japanese treatment — grated white radish and a citrus-soy dressing instead of gravy. Cuts the richness completely.

items.en: Fried chicken in sweet vinegar sauce with tartare
items.note: A Miyazaki invention now eaten nationwide: battered chicken dunked in sweet-sour vinegar sauce, then buried under egg tartare. Sweet, sharp and rich all at once.

items.en: Ginger-fried pork over rice
items.note: Thin pork slices fried with grated ginger, soy and mirin — the definitive Japanese home dinner. Soy-based, so wheat.

items.en: Four pieces of Japanese fried chicken with rice
items.note: Marinated in soy and ginger, starch-dusted, fried. Five-piece version ¥760.

items.en: Grilled beef in yakiniku sauce over rice
items.note: Sliced beef fried in the sweet soy-garlic sauce used at Japanese barbecue restaurants.

items.en: Pork and aubergine stir-fried in miso
items.note: Aubergine soaks up the miso and the pork fat and goes silky. One of the better-value hot boxes here. Miso contains wheat in most commercial blends.

items.en: Children's bento
items.note: Small portions of the mild favourites — typically fried chicken, a small hamburg, sausage and rice.

items.en: Breaded pork cutlet simmered with onion and egg over rice
items.note: The cutlet is cooked a second time in a sweet soy-dashi broth with onion, then set with beaten egg and slid over rice. Soft, sweet and savoury — nothing stays crisp, and that is the point.

items.en: Chicken and egg simmered over rice
items.note: 'Parent and child' — chicken and egg in the same bowl. The gentlest thing on this menu. With a raw egg yolk on top (tsukimi) it is ¥600.

items.en: Braised pork belly slices over rice
items.note: The same rolled, soy-braised pork that tops ramen, laid over rice with its sauce. ¥650 with a soft egg.

items.en: Japanese beef curry with rice
items.note: Japanese curry is thick, sweet and mild — closer to a brown stew than an Indian curry — and it is thickened with a wheat-flour roux, so never gluten-free. Pork-cutlet version ¥850.

items.en: Japanese curry with a breaded pork loin cutlet on top
items.note: The full comfort order. Cutlet, curry, rice.

items.en: Japanese-Chinese fried rice
items.note: Egg, spring onion and small pieces of pork, fried with soy. Sold as a side, but it is a meal.

items.en: Fried wheat noodles in sweet-savoury sauce
items.note: Steamed wheat noodles fried with cabbage and pork in a thick fruity-brown yakisoba sauce, usually topped with green nori and pickled ginger. Festival food.

items.en: Hot udon topped with a battered tube-shaped fishcake
items.note: Chikuwa is fish paste steamed around a rod so it comes out as a hollow tube; here it is battered and dropped on the noodles, where it soaks up the broth. The cheapest hot meal on the menu.

toba_kissa_shiosai.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. The morning menu below is published by Ise-Wan Ferry, the operator of the terminal; the coffee price is from a 2024 customer report. No full drinks list is posted anywhere. Open 7:40–17:40; the morning service runs 7:40–11:00 and can be taken away onto the boat.

items.ja: たまごサンドイッチ モーニングサービス
items.en: Egg sandwich morning set: sandwich, salad and a drink
items.section: モーニングサービス / Morning sets
items.note: 'Morning service' is a Tokai-region institution: order a drink before 11:00 and food comes with it for almost nothing. Japanese egg sandwiches are made with a soft mayonnaise-heavy egg filling on crustless white bread. Drink is your choice of coffee, tea or orange juice. This café sits on the 2nd floor of the Toba ferry terminal, so it is the natural stop before the Irago boat.

items.ja: ハムサンドイッチ モーニングサービス
items.en: Ham sandwich morning set: sandwich, salad and a drink
items.section: モーニングサービス / Morning sets
items.note: The same set with ham. Choose coffee, black tea or orange juice.

items.ja: トースト モーニングサービス
items.en: Toast morning set: thick-cut toast, salad and a drink
items.section: モーニングサービス / Morning sets
items.note: Japanese café toast is a single very thick slice, buttered. The plainest of the three sets.

items.en: Hot coffee
items.note: Ordered on its own outside morning hours. A ferry-terminal coffee with a view of the boats — modest, cheap, and exactly what it needs to be.

toba_sea_lounge_s_y_m.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. No menu is posted online by the shop; every price below comes from dated customer reports (2022–2025). Toba's tourism association notes the café also offers 'various set meals' that are not documented anywhere. Open 07:00–17:00, closed Wednesdays. You order at the counter, sit where you like and are called to collect; you pay on the way out.

items.en: Morning set: toast, fried egg and a drink
items.note: The reason to come. Served from 07:00 on the 2nd floor of the Toba Marine Terminal, with the whole of Toba Bay and the island ferries in front of you. Customers consistently describe it as a generous plate for the money — thick toast, a fried egg and a drink.

items.en: Japanese curry with rice
items.note: Reported in 2025 as long-simmered, with the vegetables and meat cooked down into the sauce. Japanese curry is thickened with a wheat-flour roux, so never gluten-free.

items.en: Ise udon — very soft fat wheat noodles in dark sweet tamari tare
items.note: The Ise-Shima speciality, and nothing like ordinary udon: the noodles are boiled for an hour until they lose all bite, and instead of soup there is only a small pool of near-black sweet tamari sauce at the bottom of the bowl, which you stir through. Pilgrims to Ise Jingu ate it because it was quick and easy on the stomach. Usually topped with spring onion, sometimes an egg. The tare normally contains bonito.

items.en: Canned beer
items.note: Yes, at a ferry-terminal café from 7am. Barley beer, so not gluten-free.

toba_yuki.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. No menu found.
